topic: Microsoft AZ-305 Designing Microsoft Azure Infrastructure Solutions certification exam preparation - designing identity, governance and monitoring solutions; designing data storage solutions; designing business continuity solutions; and designing infrastructure solutions on Azure, including exam case studies
cert_name: Microsoft Certified: Azure Solutions Architect Expert
exam_format: Approximately 40-60 items, 120 minutes, passing score 700/1000, delivered at Pearson VUE test centers or online-proctored via OnVUE. Question types include multiple choice (single and multi-answer), drag-and-drop, hot-area, build-list, and CASE STUDIES (multi-question scenarios grounded in a described organization) - the case studies are a defining feature of this exam. This is an EXPERT-level certification; Microsoft recommends the AZ-104 Azure Administrator credential (or equivalent) as a prerequisite. The certification renews annually via a free online Microsoft Learn assessment. The exam fee is approximately USD 165 and varies by region; present any fee as approximate and advise candidates to confirm current Microsoft pricing.
question_types: multiple choice (single answer, exactly 4 options) and multiple response clearly marked as 'Select TWO/THREE', plus case-study-style scenario questions asking which Azure design best satisfies a described set of business and technical requirements - NOT service definitions
audience: Azure solutions architects, cloud architects, senior cloud/infrastructure engineers, and technical leads who design solutions on Microsoft Azure. Microsoft recommends prior Azure administration experience (AZ-104 level) and familiarity with compute, network, storage, security, identity, and governance on Azure. Candidates should be comfortable translating business requirements into secure, scalable, reliable Azure architectures. A strong Azure companion to the Google Professional Cloud Architect course and the DP-600/AI catalog already in this catalog.
author: Aseem Mankotia

domains.name: Design identity, governance, and monitoring solutions
domains.notes: Designing the identity and control plane: authentication and authorization with Microsoft Entra ID (hybrid identity and Microsoft Entra Connect, Conditional Access, MFA, managed identities, B2B and B2C, app registrations), and RBAC including custom roles and Privileged Identity Management (PIM). Governance: management groups, subscription and resource-group topology, Azure Policy and initiatives, landing zones/Blueprints, resource locks, tags, and cost management. Monitoring and observability: Azure Monitor, Log Analytics workspaces, Application Insights, alerts, and workbooks. Choosing the correct identity, governance, or monitoring design for a described organizational requirement.

domains.name: Design data storage solutions
domains.notes: Designing storage for a described workload: relational options (Azure SQL Database, SQL Managed Instance, SQL Server on Azure VMs, Azure Database for PostgreSQL/MySQL Flexible Server) including scale, HA, and purchasing models; non-relational (Azure Cosmos DB - APIs, consistency levels, partitioning, RU sizing; Azure Table and Blob Storage). Storage accounts: performance tiers, access tiers, redundancy (LRS/ZRS/GRS/RA-GRS), lifecycle management, and immutability. Data integration and movement (Azure Data Factory, Synapse). Choosing the right data store and configuration for scale, consistency, latency, cost, and compliance.

domains.name: Design business continuity solutions
domains.notes: Designing for resilience and recovery: backup and restore (Azure Backup, backup policies, vaults), disaster recovery and replication (Azure Site Recovery/ASR, geo-redundant designs, region pairs), high availability (availability zones and sets, load balancing, multi-region active/active vs active/passive), and data archiving/retention. Meeting a described RPO/RTO and SLA. Choosing the correct BC/DR design for a stated continuity requirement.

domains.name: Design infrastructure solutions
domains.notes: The heaviest domain. Designing compute (Azure VMs and Virtual Machine Scale Sets, Azure Kubernetes Service and container options, Azure App Service, Azure Functions/serverless, Azure Container Apps, Batch); application architecture (messaging and eventing with Service Bus, Event Grid, Event Hubs, and Storage Queues; API Management; caching with Azure Cache for Redis; Logic Apps); networking (VNet and subnet design, hybrid connectivity with VPN Gateway and ExpressRoute, load-balancing selection across Azure Load Balancer, Application Gateway, Azure Front Door, and Traffic Manager, private endpoints and Private Link, NSGs, DNS); and migration (Azure Migrate, Azure Database Migration Service). Matching a described workload to the correct Azure compute, application, and network design.

extra_guidance: Microsoft AZ-305 (Azure Solutions Architect Expert) is Microsoft's flagship Azure architecture credential and a high-value, high-salary cert. It is HEAVILY scenario- and CASE-STUDY-based - the real skill it tests is 'given these business requirements plus these technical constraints, design the correct Azure architecture,' NOT reciting service definitions. Make every chapter decision-oriented. CRITICAL: the exam uses CASE STUDIES (multi-question scenarios about a described company), so include case-study-style walkthroughs and make the final chapter's simulation practice case-study pacing. Use EXACT current Azure product names: Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD), Entra Connect, Conditional Access, PIM, RBAC, management groups, Azure Policy, landing zones, Azure Monitor, Log Analytics, Application Insights, Azure SQL Database/Managed Instance, Azure Database for PostgreSQL/MySQL Flexible Server, Azure Cosmos DB, Blob/Table Storage, storage redundancy (LRS/ZRS/GRS), Azure Backup, Azure Site Recovery, availability zones, Azure VMs/Scale Sets, AKS, App Service, Azure Functions, Container Apps, Service Bus, Event Grid, Event Hubs, API Management, Azure Cache for Redis, VNet, VPN Gateway, ExpressRoute, Azure Load Balancer, Application Gateway, Azure Front Door, Traffic Manager, Private Link/private endpoints, and Azure Migrate - with a one-line note that Azure names evolve (e.g., Azure AD to Microsoft Entra ID), so verify against current docs. The four domain names and weight RANGES above are Microsoft's current skills-measured outline (April 17, 2026 update); present the percentages as the official ranges and say Microsoft gives ranges, not fixed splits. Note the AZ-104 prerequisite and the free annual Microsoft Learn renewal. Labs are READ-AND-UNDERSTAND architecture design walkthroughs (design a hub-and-spoke network, choose Load Balancer vs Application Gateway vs Front Door vs Traffic Manager, pick Cosmos DB consistency and partitioning, design an AKS vs App Service vs Functions solution, design a multi-region BC/DR with ASR, design Entra ID Conditional Access) - the exam is about architectural judgment, not portal clicks; make that explicit. Cover the classic AZ-305 traps: the four load-balancing services and when to use each, storage redundancy options, Cosmos DB consistency levels, availability zones vs sets, VPN vs ExpressRoute, managed identities vs service principals, Azure Policy vs RBAC, and RPO/RTO-driven DR choices. NEVER promise a pass or use the word 'guarantee' in ANY form (Udemy compliance) - use 'exam-focused preparation' framing throughout, including learning objectives and who-this-is-for. Present the exam fee as approximate (~USD 165, varies by region) and advise verifying current Microsoft pricing and the latest skills-measured guide. The final chapter must be a full exam simulation with a 120-minute, case-study-pacing time-management strategy. Scan the practice bank for stray other-vendor terms (AWS/Google/NVIDIA) before upload per the pipeline compliance rules.
